audits.title: Improving the practice of handover for psychiatric inpatient nursing staff.
audits.standard: SBAR communication framework for nursing handover
audits.setting: 27 inpatient psychiatric units, Centre for Addiction and Mental Health, Toronto

cycle1.result: SBAR used in 4% of handovers; satisfaction with handover information 34%.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles: psychiatry-relevant SBAR resources developed, staff education, audits and survey.
audits.citation: Abela-Dimech F, Vuksic O. Improving the practice of handover for psychiatric inpatient nursing staff. Arch Psychiatr Nurs. 2018;32(5):729-736. doi:10.1016/j.apnu.2018.04.004. PMID: 30201201.

audits.title: Clinical nursing handovers for continuity of safe patient care in adult surgical wards: a best practice implementation project.
audits.standard: JBI PACES audit criteria for clinical handover
audits.setting: Three adult surgical wards, tertiary hospital (National University Hospital)

cycle1.result: Handovers using standardised documentation 0%; detailed observations 72.7%; relevant history 93.9%.

audits.intervention: Adequate staffing during handovers, structured standardised handover, visual cues and a teaching video.

cycle2.result: Standardised documentation 21.0% (p = 0.005); detailed observations 87.9%; relevant history 97.0%.

audits.other_findings: Handover-related medication error incidents fell by 72% over six months.
audits.citation: Wong X, Tung YJ, Peck SY, Goh ML. Clinical nursing handovers for continuity of safe patient care in adult surgical wards: a best practice implementation project. JBI Database System Rev Implement Rep. 2019;17(5):1003-1015. doi:10.11124/jbisrir-2017-004024. PMID: 31090654.

audits.title: Shift-to-shift handoffs in the NICU: lessons learned from a large scale audit.
audits.standard: Handoff audit tool outlining best practice behaviours
audits.setting: 40 NICU centres in a learning collaborative

cycle1.result: Many behaviours demonstrated reliably, with differences between nurse and provider handoffs; families present for 5.9% of handoffs, and 48.2% of those present participated.

audits.citation: Kaplan HC, Timpson W, Meyers J, Schierholz E, Cohen H, Fry M, et al.. Shift-to-shift handoffs in the NICU: lessons learned from a large scale audit. J Perinatol. 2023;43(12):1468-1473. doi:10.1038/s41372-023-01724-2. PMID: 37452115.

audits.title: General principles of communication among nurses in a long-term care unit: a best practice implementation project.
audits.standard: Three JBI audit criteria: communication training, teamwork/conflict training and use of a structured tool (ISBAR) at handover
audits.setting: Long-term care unit, Hospital José Luciano de Castro, Anadia

cycle1.result: Communication training 0%; teamwork and conflict training 21%; ISBAR use at handover 43.6%.

audits.intervention: Educational sessions and a focus group; ISBAR adapted for the unit.

cycle2.result: Communication training 78%; teamwork and conflict training 50%; ISBAR use 91%.

audits.other_findings: Baseline included 250 observed handovers and a questionnaire of 14 nurses.
audits.citation: Felizardo H, Cardoso D, Nogueira P, Bastos J, Casimiro D, Nogueira P, et al.. General principles of communication among nurses in a long-term care unit: a best practice implementation project. JBI Evid Implement. 2025;23(S1):S1-S8. doi:10.1097/xeb.0000000000000482. PMID: 39792628.

audits.title: Communicating Safely: Standardizing Nursing Clinical Reports in a Neonatal Unit.
audits.standard: Recommended ISOAP (Introduction, Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) format for nursing handover reports
audits.setting: Tertiary Neonatal Intensive Care and Special Care Nursery, Centenary Hospital for Women and Children, Canberra
audits.intervention: Two PDSA cycles (paper-based then digital health records): neonatal-specific ISOAP templates, education sessions, peer mentorship, visual reminders and ongoing staff support

cycle2.result: Adherence 78% by January 2022 and 100% by March 2022; after DHR transition adherence improved from 65% in May 2023 to 92% by July 2023

audits.other_findings: Staff reported improved clarity, communication, reduced time for clinical reviews and greater satisfaction.
audits.citation: Broom M, Briguglio L, Sam M, Grlj L, Martinoski J, O'Brien C. Communicating Safely: Standardizing Nursing Clinical Reports in a Neonatal Unit. Adv Neonatal Care. 2026;26(3):255-260. doi:10.1097/anc.0000000000001359. PMID: 41955629.

audits.title: Investigating the impact of nursing shift change audit on the safety of emergency department patients.
audits.setting: Emergency department of a hospital in Tehran

cycle1.result: Mean SBAR score 21.31 before intervention (35 nurses, 70 patients).

audits.intervention: Theoretical training sessions on the SBAR method and a training video, with review of problems.

cycle2.result: Mean SBAR score 49.49 after intervention (significant increase).

audits.other_findings: Patient safety and nurse satisfaction were also assessed by questionnaire.
audits.citation: Kazemi S, Hashemi S, Rahmani A, Mahmoudi H. Investigating the impact of nursing shift change audit on the safety of emergency department patients. Int Emerg Nurs. 2025;78:101551. doi:10.1016/j.ienj.2024.101551. PMID: 39642759.
